name: SGAS J003341.5+024217 (Hubble)
blurb: SGAS J003341.5+024217, a gravitationally lensed galaxy with an active nucleus, seen by Hubble.
label: sgas20033-hubble
story: The gravity of a foreground cluster of galaxies stretches a distant galaxy into a long arc and two extra images, with a feeding black hole driving an outflow from its core. Hubble mapped its glowing gas to tell the light of newborn stars apart from the glow stirred up by the black hole.

claims.text: It is a lensed galaxy hosting a Seyfert active galactic nucleus
It is multiply imaged as an elongated arc and two counter images
The lens is a sub-cluster offset from the core of a main galaxy cluster
It hosts an AGN-driven nuclear outflow, and Hubble mapped emission to separate star formation from AGN ionization
